THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, JUNE 10, 1936
149c
Share Forfeiture Rules
Leave No Option To The
Directors Of Companies

Important Provision Of China Orders-In-Council
Overlooked; Newmilks, Ltd., Seek Relief
From Liability To Heavy Penalties

FAVOURABLE DECISION MUST NOT BE
CONSTRUED AS A PRECEDENT

Overlooking of highly important provisions of the
China Orders-in-Council, that failure by would-be share-
holders to meet their liabilities on share subscriptions at the
specified times renders their shares automatically forfeit
and that Companies have no option but to declare such
shares forfeit and to file a return of forfeitures with the
Registrar of Companies, led to an application before Judge
P. Grant Jones in H. M. Supreme Court yesterday, seeking
relief from the penalties imposed for non-compliance.

It was the first case of its kind brought before the
Court and it concerned the firm of Newmilks, Limited, which
had, it was admitted, permitted many of its shares to be
fully paid up by the original applicants long after the
specified term of three months allowed after allotment on
part-payment. The Company was formed in June, 1934, and
the Directors permitted certain shareholders to delay making
their final payments up to May, 1935.

Mr. John McNeill, of Hansons,
appeared for the Company, and
Mr. Victor Priestwood, Crown
Advocate, represented the Re-
gistrar of Companies.

The motion and an affidavit by
Mr. H. W. Howell, secretary and
of Newmilks, Ltd., were read by
Mr. McNeill, in which it was
pleaded that the Directors were
not aware of the actual provisions
of the Order-in-Council and that
the failure to comply was due to
inadvertence.

It was supposed that failure of
applicants for shares to pay the
balance due rendered the shares
allotted liable to forfeiture, but
that action declaring them forfeit
was optional.

Provisions Peculiar To China
Mr. McNeill pointed out that
persons starting a new Company
would make reference to the
Hongkong Ordinances, but unless
their attention was specifically
drawn to the provisions of the
Orders-in-Council they might
easily be overlooked.

Judge Grant Jones: Is it a fact
that the Orders-in-Council are
peculiar to our jurisdiction?

Mr. Priestwood: Yes, my Lord.

Judge Grant Jones: That would
seem to be a point in your favour,
Mr. McNeill.

He stated, however, that he
regarded a breach of the Orders
as a much more serious offence
than an infringement of the
Companies Ordinance.

Mr. McNeill said that cash had
been received for all
the shares except 50 issued to
a Director, which had been
paid up, and he urged
that the Court should grant relief.

Judge Grant Jones: Not until
you have done what you ought to
have done. Not only have you
not declared the shares forfeit,
but you have still received pay-
ment on them. You have stultified
the law.

Mr. McNeill: The Article
provides that a certain thing
shall be done, that the shares
shall be forfeited, but the share-
holders are not called upon by
the Article to be aware of its
provisions, to know that their
shares must be forfeited on non-
payment at the specified time.
They have put their money in
afterwards in good faith. It
would be a grave injustice if they
were called upon to forfeit their
shares now.

Judge Grant Jones: The Com-
pany might be required to return
money received illegally.

Mr. McNeill: That might be
all right if the Company were
not in a state of insolvency.

Judge Grant Jones: But do we
have to consider that? It is not
before the Court in this applica-
tion. The money should be repaid.

Company Condemnation
Mr. McNeill went on to argue
that on allotment of shares a
contract was entered into between
the parties and that if the time
for fulfilment was extended, the
contract remained a legal one.

Judge Grant Jones: You say
the Company condones?

Mr. McNeill: Yes.

Judge Grant Jones: I don't see
that that is any excuse. They
are acting against the law. The
various payments made for noth-
ing. On a matter of principle I
think it is a very important
case. I don't think relief can be
granted until petitioners have
done what they ought to have
done. I understand the
position of the Company does not
warrant me in granting relief.
This is a case where the Directors
ought to have known better.

feited. It is no excuse that the
Company has waived a provision
of its share issue.

Reason For Provision
Mr. McNeill submitted that the
Article must be considered broad-
ly. It must have been inserted for
the protection of the public. In
this case no-one had been harmed.
No misconception had been allow-
ed to arise in the mind of any
creditor.

Judge Grant Jones: But we
cannot go behind the wording of
the Article.

Mr. McNeill: I submit that you
are entitled to go behind it. You
are entitled to look for the reason
for its insertion. There must be
one and I suggest it is the pro-
tection of the public.

"If these shares had not sub-
sequently been paid up, it might
have been said that the creditors
were injured, but they were paid
up and nobody has been harmed."

"The law cannot be interpreted
to the detriment of the public.
The present shareholders have
held their shares for two years.

股份没收规则
公司董事别无选择

《中国枢密院令》重要条款被忽视；纽米尔克斯有限公司（Newmilks, Ltd.）寻求免除巨额罚款责任

有利判决不得被视为先例

由于忽视了《中国枢密院令》中极为重要的条款——即准股东未在规定时间履行认股缴款义务将导致其股份自动没收，且公司除宣布此类股份没收并向公司注册官提交没收报告外别无选择——导致昨日在英王陛下最高法院向格兰特·琼斯（P. Grant Jones）法官提出申请，寻求免除因违规而施加的处罚。

这是提交至法院的首宗此类案件，涉及纽米尔克斯有限公司（Newmilks, Limited）。该公司承认，允许许多原始申请人在部分配股后规定的三个月期限届满很久之后，才缴清全部股款。该公司成立于1934年6月，董事允许某些股东将最终付款延迟至1935年5月。

汉森律师事务所（Hansons）的约翰·麦克尼尔（John McNeill）先生代表公司出庭，王室律师维克多·普里斯特伍德（Victor Priestwood）先生代表公司注册官。

麦克尼尔先生宣读了动议以及纽米尔克斯有限公司秘书兼[职位原文缺失或不清] H. W. 豪厄尔（H. W. Howell）先生的宣誓书，其中辩称董事们并不知晓该枢密院令的实际规定，违规行为系出于疏忽。

人们曾认为，认股申请人未能支付余额会导致已配股份面临没收风险，但宣布没收的行动是可选的。

中国特有的条款

麦克尼尔先生指出，创办新公司的人通常会参考香港条例，但如果他们的注意力没有被特别引导至枢密院令的条款上，这些条款很容易被忽视。

格兰特·琼斯法官：枢密院令是我们司法辖区所特有的，这是事实吗？

普里斯特伍德先生：是的，法官大人。

格兰特·琼斯法官：这似乎对你有利，麦克尼尔先生。

然而，他表示，他认为违反枢密院令比违反《公司条例》是更为严重的罪行。

麦克尼尔先生说，除发给一名董事的50股已缴清外，所有股份的现金均已收到，他恳请法院给予宽免。

格兰特·琼斯法官：除非你们做了本该做的事。你们不仅没有宣布股份没收，甚至还继续收取这些股份的款项。你们使法律变得荒谬无效。

麦克尼尔先生：该条款规定必须做某事，即股份应被没收，但该条款并未要求股东知晓其规定，即知道如果不在规定时间付款，他们的股份必须被没收。他们后来是出于善意投入资金的。如果现在要求他们没收股份，将是极大的不公。

格兰特·琼斯法官：公司可能被要求退还非法收到的款项。

麦克尼尔先生：如果公司没有处于资不抵债的状态，那或许可以。

格兰特·琼斯法官：但我们必须考虑这一点吗？在本申请中，这并非法院审理的范围。这笔钱应当退还。

公司的纵容

麦克尼尔先生继续辩称，在配股时，双方之间订立了合同，如果履行期限被延长，合同仍然是合法的。

格兰特·琼斯法官：你是说公司予以宽恕（condones）？

麦克尼尔先生：是的。

格兰特·琼斯法官：我不认为这是什么借口。他们的行为违背法律。各种付款都白付了。从原则上来讲，我认为这是一个非常重要的案件。我认为，在申请人完成他们本该做的事情之前，不能给予宽免。我理解，公司的状况并不能证明我有理由给予宽免。这是一个董事们本应更清楚情况的案件。

[原文此处有残缺或排版错误，接上文语意] ...没收。公司放弃其股份发行的一项条款，并不能成为借口。

条款存在的理由

麦克尼尔先生提出，必须从广义上考虑该条款。其插入必定是为了保护公众利益。在本案中，没有人受到伤害。任何债权人的心中都没有产生误解。

格兰特·琼斯法官：但我们不能脱离条款的字面含义去探究。

麦克尼尔先生：我提请您有权探究其背后原因。您有权寻找插入该条款的理由。必定有一个理由，我认为那就是保护公众。

“如果这些股份随后未被缴清，可能会说债权人受到了损害，但它们已被缴清，没有人受到伤害。”

“法律的解释不能以损害公众利益为代价。现有股东持有其股份已有两年。如果现在没收他们的股份，对任何人都没有帮助。他们有权获得法院的体谅。”

格兰特·琼斯法官：他们知道自己已经逾期。

麦克尼尔先生：假设这是正确的，这仍然不是解释该条款的合理方式。现在没收股份只会惩罚那些随后履行了合同的股东，这对任何人都没有帮助。

“该条款规定，董事应宣布股份没收，如果不这样做，将面临严厉处罚，因为如果允许未 fully paid（全额缴付）的股份被视为已全额缴付，可能会损害公众利益。在本案中，股份已全额缴付，我请求免除处罚。现在没收股份是完全不合理的。”

关于过失问题，他只能说他们只能乞求法院的怜悯，直白地说：“我们不会再犯。”

他敦促说，如果没有造成损害，就不应严格执行该条款。如果造成了损害，是的，否则则不然。

注册官的立场

普里斯特伍德先生说，虽然鉴于本案的特殊情况，他并不反对该申请，但这是一个需要非常谨慎处理的案件。

他说，第199条的插入似乎是考虑到这样一个事实：一家中国公司的股东可能属于一个或半打不同的国籍，而试图收购股份的人可能被迫在六个不同的法院提起诉讼。

因此，决定未履行的股份义务应导致其自动没收。

他进一步指出，如果纽米尔克斯

有限公司（Limited）的董事在应该的时候宣布股份没收，他们就可以按面值重新发行这些股份，债权人甚至可能从被没收的资金中受益。这可能是一个卑鄙的手段……

格兰特·琼斯法官：这并不卑鄙。根据枢密院令，董事被迫没收股份。这是一个合理的论点。

麦克尼尔先生说这纯粹是假设性的。没有任何义务迫使董事重新发行。他们可能在持有被没收的资金时，发现只需重新发行一半的股份就能获得所需的全部资本。债权人不会受到损害，因为只有在所有债权人都得到清偿后，股东才会获得支付。

法官的评论

格兰特·琼斯法官指出，该动议旨在寻求免除1925年《中国枢密院令》第199条所施加的处罚，他说，在他看来，这与根据英国和香港公司法申请宽免完全是两回事。

“所承认的无知，并不是对一部冗长复杂的法规中少数几个章节的无知。而是对我们在这个国家生活和贸易所依据的《枢密院令》中少数几个条款的无知。

“第199条并没有明确赋予延期的权力，申请人的律师已放弃动议中的这一部分。然而，该条款确实授权法院在认为在所有情况下均公正时，免除处罚。

“这里的情况表明，遗漏并未造成实际损害，如果不给予公司所寻求的宽免，可能会造成潜在损害。

“王室律师关于债权人可能受到损害的论点给我留下了深刻印象，但申请人律师提到的观点表明情况并非如此，即在任何清算中，债权人都优先于股东。

“在所有情况下，我准备在此案中给予宽免，但这绝不得被视为先例，因为我不确定我是否在略微偏向公司一方。

“这种无知是严重的疏忽。这就是旧法律书籍中所称的‘crassa negligentia’（重大过失），我希望不要再有其他案例提交到我面前。我正在考虑公司注册官未出庭这一事实。”

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, JUNE 3, 1936
14786.
Affairs Of Newmilks Limited
Discussed In H.M. Court
Creditor's Petition For Winding-Up Ordered To
Stand Over Pending Negotiations For
Sale As A Going Concern

A petition by Mr. Max Morris Engel, judgment creditor, for the compulsory winding-up of Newmilks Limited, manufacturers and distributors of milk, cream and soya food products, was submitted in H.M. Supreme Court before Judge Grant Jones yesterday.

On evidence by Mr. H. W. Howell, managing director, that negotiations are proceeding for the reorganisation or sale of the business as a going concern, the Court made an order for the winding-up petition to stand over for a month, with liberty to apply.

Mr. C. E. Lowe appeared for the petitioner and Mr. K. E. Newman, who opposed the petition, for the Receiver appointed by the debenture holders, for the landlord and for Mr. Howell on behalf of the staff.

The facts set out in the petition read by Mr. Lowe were to the effect that Newmilks, Ltd. commenced business in June, 1934, with head offices at 60 Nanzing Road, with an authorized capital of $500,000, of which $226,500 had been issued and paid-up.

On March 9 this year, Mr. Engel obtained judgment against the company for $3,000 amount due to him for commission. On March 11 he issued a writ of execution, but the judgment had not been satisfied.

The Company, it was submitted, was unable to pay its debts.

Mr. Lowe pointed out that a Company was considered to be unable to pay its debts if an execution of judgment was returned unsatisfied in whole or in part. The affidavit was prima facie proof, he submitted.

Debenture Holders' Rights

Mr. Newman said that the opposition were not disputing the facts set out in the affidavit. He was relying on the fact that a Receiver had been appointed by the debenture holders. He submitted that this was sufficient on the authority of H. Pounds and Sons v. Hutchins to dispose of the petition. In that case, it was held that the Court had no right to interfere with the powers of the debenture holders.

He submitted that it was not left to the Court to decide. The debenture holders were able to come and say: It is within our power to appoint a Receiver and we have appointed him.

Judge Grant Jones: The case is not in point. You have to satisfy me that the Company should not be wound up. Your affidavit merely shows the position of the debenture holders after a winding-up order has already been made.

Mr. Newman: We say we now own the whole property and we have taken possession. You cannot turn us out.

Judge Grant Jones: I am afraid the authorities are against you.

Three Receivers

Mr. Howell told the Court that 25,000 first mortgage debentures were issued in August last and that the holders exercised their powers to take possession on March 13 when Mr. E. Remedios was appointed Receiver. Witness was appointed Receiver on April 2 when Mr. Remedios resigned, and on May 28, Mr. J. E. Turner took over the position.

The Company, through its Receiver, had recently borrowed further money to enable it to carry on. Further debentures for $10,800 were issued, ranking prior to the others. They were all issued to the China Finance Corporation. All but $4,300 had since been paid off.

The advances were made for the purpose of keeping the business going. If it had to be sold a much higher price could be obtained if it kept running than if it became defunct.

Questioned by the Court, Mr. Howell estimated the liabilities of the Company at approximately $80,000, including $50,000 sundry creditors and sum owing to the debenture holders.

Mr. Newman: In your opinion, if the Company is given sufficient time, is it likely to be sold as a going concern.

Mr. Howell: I don't think anybody would dispute that if it is saved from disaster now and is not involved in any further litigation, it could be made to pay its way very easily.

Judge Grant Jones: Then why not pay Mr. Engels his $3,000 and end the matter.

Witness: If I did there would be a storm from the other creditors.

Some Ill-feeling

Mr. Newman asked the Court, on this evidence, to order the petition to stand over. He pointed out that there were other heavy creditors of the Company and that Mr. Engels was the only one trying to force the Company into liquidation.

Judge Grant Jones: I gather there is some ill-feeling between the parties.

Mr. Howell, replying to a further question, said negotiations were now in progress with a syndicate to sell Newmilks, Limited, as a going concern. He thought the result, one way or the other, would be known within a month.

Mr. Lowe: Since the judgment on March 9, have you tried to pay Mr. Engel anything?—No.

Did you try to pay by instalments?—No.

I suggest you have never made any attempt to pay him?—No.

On the contrary, we have used whatever money we received from the debtors to keep the business going, supplying its customers.

He stated that if the business was stopped for one day, the petitioner would not get one penny.

Judge Grant Jones: There is the position, Mr. Lowe. If you can rely upon Mr. Howell, the making of an order for winding-up will mean that your client will not get a penny. If I order a stand-over, he will take his chance of getting a penny or a penny-halfpenny at a later date.

The order was later made by consent.

新牛奶有限公司（Newmilks Limited）事务
在英国驻华法院审理
债权人提出的清盘申请获准搁置，以待就作为持续经营企业出售一事进行谈判

昨日，判决债权人马克斯·莫里斯·恩格尔先生（Mr. Max Morris Engel）向英国驻华最高法院提交了一份申请，要求对生产及分销牛奶、奶油和大豆制品的新牛奶有限公司（Newmilks Limited）进行强制清盘。该案由格兰特·琼斯法官（Judge Grant Jones）审理。

鉴于总经理H. W. 豪厄尔先生（Mr. H. W. Howell）提供的证据表明，目前正就重组业务或将其作为持续经营的企业出售进行谈判，法院下令将清盘申请搁置一个月，并保留各方再次申请的权利。

C. E. 洛先生（Mr. C. E. Lowe）代表申请人出庭；K. E. 纽曼先生（Mr. K. E. Newman）反对该申请，他代表由债券持有人委任的接管人、房东以及代表职员的豪厄尔先生出庭。

洛先生宣读的申请书中陈述的事实大意如下：新牛奶有限公司于1934年6月开始营业，总部设在南京路60号，法定资本为50万美元，其中已发行并缴足226,500美元。

今年3月9日，恩格尔先生因公司欠付其佣金3,000美元而获得针对该公司的胜诉判决。3月11日，他发出了执行令，但该判决尚未得到履行。

据称，该公司无力偿还债务。

洛先生指出，如果判决执行令全部或部分未能得到履行，则公司被视为无力偿还债务。他提出，该宣誓书即构成表面证据。

债券持有人的权利

纽曼先生说，反对方并不否认宣誓书中陈述的事实。他依据的事实是，债券持有人已委任了一名接管人。他提出，根据 H. Pounds and Sons v. Hutchins 一案的判例，这足以驳回该申请。在该案中，法院裁定其无权干涉债券持有人的权力。

他提出，此事并非由法院决定。债券持有人可以出来说：我们有权委任接管人，且我们已委任了他。

格兰特·琼斯法官：该案与本案情形不符。你必须使我信服该公司不应被清盘。你的宣誓书仅显示了在已经作出清盘令之后债券持有人的处境。

纽曼先生：我们要说的是，我们现在拥有全部财产，并且已经接管。你不能将我们赶走。

格兰特·琼斯法官：恐怕判例对你不利。

三位接管人

豪厄尔先生告诉法院，去年8月发行了25,000股第一抵押债券，持有人于3月13日行使权力接管公司，当时委任E. 雷梅迪奥斯先生（Mr. E. Remedios）为接管人。证人于4月2日雷梅迪奥斯先生辞职后被委任为接管人，随后于5月28日由J. E. 特纳先生（Mr. J. E. Turner）接任该职位。

该公司通过其接管人最近又借入资金以维持运营。又发行了面值10,800美元的债券，其受偿顺序优先于其他债券。这些债券全部发行给中国金融公司（China Finance Corporation）。除4,300美元外，其余款项此后均已偿还。

预付款项的目的是为了维持业务运转。如果必须出售，保持运营状态比停业清算能获得高得多的价格。

经法院询问，豪厄尔先生估计公司的负债约为80,000美元，其中包括50,000美元的其他债权人欠款及欠债券持有人的款项。

纽曼先生：在你看来，如果给予公司足够的时间，它是否有可能作为持续经营的企业被出售？

豪厄尔先生：我认为无人会否认，如果现在能使其免于灾难，且不卷入进一步的诉讼，它很容易就能实现收支平衡。

格兰特·琼斯法官：那为何不支付恩格斯先生3,000美元以了结此事呢？

证人：如果我那样做，其他债权人就会掀起风波。

一些不和情绪

纽曼先生基于上述证据，请求法院命令搁置该申请。他指出，公司还有其他大额债权人，而恩格斯先生是唯一试图迫使公司进入清算程序的人。

格兰特·琼斯法官：我推测双方之间存在一些不和情绪。
